name: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
dates: Kept since 1263; on this date since 1969
history: Soon after the Annunciation, Mary went in haste to the hill country of Judah to visit her kinswoman Elizabeth, who was carrying John the Baptist. At Mary’s greeting the child leapt in Elizabeth’s womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, called her blessed among women. Mary answered with the Magnificat, the song the Church sings every evening.
life: Saint Luke tells the story in the first chapter of his Gospel. Mary, having heard from the angel that Elizabeth had conceived in her old age, set out at once, travelling some distance to a town that tradition places at Ein Karem, near Jerusalem. Elizabeth’s words, blessed are you among women and blessed is the fruit of your womb, became part of the Hail Mary. Mary’s reply, my soul magnifies the Lord, echoes the song of Hannah and praises the God who scatters the proud and fills the hungry with good things. She stayed about three months. The Franciscans kept the feast from 1263, and Urban VI extended it to the whole Church in 1389, praying for an end to the Great Schism. It was kept on 2 July until 1969, when it moved to the last day of May, between the Annunciation and the birth of John the Baptist.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, you carried Christ in haste to your kinswoman, and the child in her womb leapt for joy. Bring Him to me and to all I meet today. Pray for expectant mothers and for the elderly, and teach me to magnify the Lord with you in every circumstance of my life. Amen.
penance: Make a visit today: to an elderly relative, an expectant mother, or someone who would value your company. Pray the Magnificat for them.
meditation: Mary did not wait to be visited; she went in haste. Who is waiting for you to come?
